¤Male Competition -Dimorphism
  nThere is a phenotypic difference between males and females of a populations
  nMale baboons larger than female
  nMale birds with flamboyant coloration (peacock vs peahen)
explanation: Sexual dimorphism refers to the phenotypic differences between males and females of the same species. This condition arises due to sexual selection pressures. The slide provides two examples of dimorphism: (1) male baboons are significantly larger than females, a trait that aids in physical competition; and (2) male birds exhibit flamboyant coloration (such as a peacock's vibrant feathers) to attract females, while females (peahens) have duller, cryptic coloration.

questions.q: What is the term for phenotypic differences between males and females of the same population?
questions.exp: Sexual dimorphism is defined as the phenotypic differences between males and females within a population.

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of sexual dimorphism described in the notes?
opts: Human babies with low birth weights
Peacocks having flamboyant coloration compared to peahens
Peppered moths changing color due to soot
questions.exp: Peacocks having flamboyant feathers while peahens are dull is a classic example of sexual dimorphism driven by sexual selection.
